I made a post about it here but the gist is that our entire society has been predicated on mass employment or mass slavery pretty much since the beginning of modern civilization. What we've seen happen in the past decades is that worker productivity has skyrocketed. If in the 50s it took 50 people to make the goods for 100 people. Those same 50 people can now make the goods for 600 people. Really. Productivity across all sectors is really up 600%! And it continues to rapidly rise. Increased automation will see exponential gains there.

This productivity means companies now need 1/6th as many workers to complete the same amount of work. The number of desirable jobs is rapidly plummeting and will continue to plummet. This is the reason you have baristas and retail workers with college degrees, and not just liberal arts. It's also the reason you see things like requiring two years work experience for entry level positions. It's also the reason the average person today is earning about as much today as they did in the 70s even though they're creating far more wealth for their company than ever before. Wifi backscatter sound complicated but in reality it is not.

In it simplest way you can visualize it like this:

  • You have your 500W light source (your normal full power wifi transmitter)
  • Your light detector (the so called wifi helper that is also a normal wifi device)
  • One or more Kindle e-readers that is hanging on you wall (your passive wifi device(s)).

Now your 500W light source has maybe 2500 lux brightness that gets received at the light detector via direct and reflected light. That 500W light source also gives enough power to a solar cell that is powering your Kindle e-reader.

The Kindle can now receive information from the 500W light source by varying the brightness just like a normal wifi signal. And because your separated light detector also receives the same variation and information by the light source how it changed brightness via normal wifi signal, it knows the signal base line. Anything that deviates from that predicted base line must come from a passive wifi device.

The big finale is this: The kindle changes its reflective screen to dark, reflective, dark, reflective,..... influencing the brightness received on the light detector. The power required to change the Kindle screen is maybe 0.1W based on the data it must transmit is maybe 0.1W which it gets from its solar panel lit by the 500W transmitter.

WiFi backscatter PDF: https://homes.cs.washington.edu/~gshyam/Papers/wifibackscatter.pdf

Note: In the example a TV screen would of course mess up the signal, but in the real case it is a radio signal, so a electronic shielded TV would be silent enough not to interfere.
